brief: J.P. Morgan's International Market Intelligence desk is tactically cautious to neutral on global equities. Asian equities and US/EU futures are mixed with Brent nearing $100 on renewed US-Iran escalation, so the desk prefers cheap EU index hedges, put spreads or hybrids, since it holds that the constructive bigger picture limits drawdowns. Regional preference stays long US and Asia over EU because the US is overheating, Europe is recovering from stagflation, and secular themes carry less weight in EU equities. Supercycle themes are the core longs, but an expected multi-week factor rotation keeps the desk hedged via momentum options while it buys dips. Shorts span AI-vulnerable names, EU Insurance and challenged industries, with high conviction on EU Chemicals and Asia Consumer Electronics. In tech the focus is the AI infrastructure and bottleneck rebound, though leadership should stay broader than in 1H26. Nishihara sees USD/JPY holding 155-160 rather than sustaining a move below 150, a range the note argues modestly helps Japanese earnings against a FY2026 guidance assumption of 153. EM is rated bullish on improving macro, weaker USD and AI capex, with divergence expected across countries and sectors. Hedge funds re-grossed while net exposure stayed muted.
